import json,hashlib,collections,time
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('/home/sdegan/space-teaching-aid/public/data'); out=Path('/tmp/space-phase2-20260920')
m=json.loads((out/'live-manifest.json').read_text())
local=json.loads((root/'manifest.json').read_text())
assert m['orbitEvents']==local['orbitEvents']
assert m['orbitHistory']==local['orbitHistory']
a=json.loads((root/m['orbitEvents']['path']).read_text()); print('live matched',m['orbitEvents'],flush=True)
selected=[]; allcounts=collections.Counter(); began=time.monotonic()
for r in m['orbitHistory']['shards']:
    raw=(root/r['path']).read_bytes();assert hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()==r['sha256']
    for obj in json.loads(raw)['objects']:
        for e in obj.get('events',[]):
            if e.get('controlBasis')!='self-history': continue
            group='passive' if e['objectType'].upper() in ('DEBRIS','ROCKET BODY') else 'payload' if e['objectType'].upper()=='PAYLOAD' else 'unknown'
            allcounts[group]+=1
            tests=[t for t in e['tests'] if t['element']=='inclination' and t['tripped']]
            if not tests: continue
            selected.append({k:e.get(k) for k in ('norad','startAt','endAt','inclinationDeg','perigeeAltitudeKm','signature','expectation','objectType')}|{'group':group,'test':tests[0]})
    if r['shard']%32==0:print('shard',r['shard'],'inclination',len(selected),flush=True)
(out/'published-inclination.json').write_text(json.dumps(selected))
(out/'published-controls.json').write_text(json.dumps(a['controls']['selfHistory'],indent=2))
print('counts',allcounts,'inclination',collections.Counter(e['group'] for e in selected),'objects',len(set(e['norad'] for e in selected)),'seconds',time.monotonic()-began)

rateSeparation.gap: The payload flag rate is only 6.9 times the false-alarm floor once both are read at their 95 per cent bounds, against the 10 times this site requires before an individual event may be called a manoeuvre. Up to one flag in 7 on a payload could be the same noise.
rateSeparation.note: Lower bound on the payload rate against upper bound on the passive rate. Bounds rather than point estimates, and an effect size rather than a p-value: with tens of millions of intervals a two-proportion test is significant for a ratio of 1.001, which would say the archive is large rather than that the detector separates the two populations.
